correctness.rationale: For finite connected undirected graph with one reset node and c,lambda>0, synchronous coupling gives an exponential L2 contraction because 2cL+lambda e_re_r^T is strictly positive. The anchored h solves cLh=omega-Omega e_r; translating by h gives universal driving Omega e_r, hence full stationary-law universality. First-moment sum gives m_r=Omega/lambda; the graph zero mode gives all other means. A quadratic-generator calculation yields the exact finite-rate covariance Lyapunov equation. Its graph-product killed-walk resolvent is strictly positive for Omega nonzero. Block Schur estimates prove C_rr=Omega^2/lambda^2+O(lambda^-3), C_rM=cOmega^2 a^T/lambda^3+O(lambda^-4), and lambda^3 C_MM -> 2cOmega^2 integral exp(-Bt)aa^T exp(-Bt)dt. Every component of G\{r} meets a, so all limiting entries are positive. The standalone program ran 140 deterministic numerical/algebraic checks on model equations, six finite graph families and an exact two-state formula. No finite computation is treated as an infinite proof.

Earlier nonlinear mean-field Kuramoto subsystem-reset papers concern different state variables and do not state the graphwise full-distribution affine frequency-sum invariance, exact second-moment equation, or strictly positive cubic covariance on never-reset nodes. Actual published-record searches returned no direct overlap. Residual generic linear jump-process coverage is explicitly disclosed; originality is assessed as best-knowledge, not an independently established priority claim.
residual_risks: An older general theorem about affine piecewise-deterministic Markov processes with coordinate resets might imply the frequency-profile translation after an unstated specialization.

The 2019 graph pinning and noise work was available only at abstract level; its full results were not excluded.

value.rationale: The work answers a physically motivated open finite-rate question left by the source infinite-reset treatment: stochastic noise received by unreset oscillators. It proves an exact all-frequency-profile universality, an exact zero-total-frequency deterministic boundary, and a sharp separation of local lambda^-2 versus propagated lambda^-3 fluctuations with a strictly positive grounded-heat-kernel prefactor at every never-reset pair. The result quantifies network-wide coherence control and shows which portion of finite-rate stochastic resetting changes deterministic phase alignment versus fluctuations. It is a structurally motivated finite-graph theorem, not a routine numerical increment or arbitrary special case.
